extracted.intended_audience: U.S. journalists, editors, photojournalists and news organizations considering entry in ASNE Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and descriptive guidance for the 2016 American Society of News Editors (ASNE) Awards categories, describing what the judges look for and who is eligible. Covers multiple award categories (e.g., Batten Medal, editorial leadership, nondeadline writing, diversity, local accountability, commentary, online storytelling, breaking news writing, photojournalism).

rubrics_metrics.name: General ASNE Awards eligibility and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The ASNE Awards honor the best in print, digital and video content in nine categories. With the exception of the Batten Medal (which covered work published since 2013), the awards were given for work completed in 2015. All news organizations, news services and online-only news sites in the United States, including those without an ASNE member on staff, were eligible to enter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contest drew more than 300 entries. Judging took place both online and on site at The Poynter Institute for Media Studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Batten Medal
rubrics_metrics.description: Honors public-service journalism in memory of James K. Batten. The medal is intended to celebrate the journalistic values Batten stood for: compassion, courage, humanity and a deep concern for the underdog.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges' remarks emphasize extraordinary efforts and risks taken to produce work, compelling storytelling, profound humanity, bearing witness to suffering, and personal courage (example: reporting that exposes the reality of women's experience in Afghanistan and chronicles Yazidi refugees, including personal risk such as surviving a helicopter crash). Winning entry example: Afghanistan reporting by Alissa Rubin of The New York Times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burl Osborne Award for Editorial Leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes editorial writing that is excellent journalism and makes a difference in a community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges note powerful and persuasive editorials that champion marginalized groups, use solid research and 'searing sentiment' to reach readers' minds and hearts, and that compel community action or change. Winning examples include editorials advocating for immigrant rights and immigration policy grounded in reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deborah Howell Award for Nondeadline Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in writing that's not accomplished on deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges look for taut, sophisticated narrative, deep character development, powerful and nuanced reporting and writing, exceptional partnership and investigative approach that may 'break conventions.' Winning example: 'An Unbelievable Story of Rape' praised for narrative craft and investigative impact showing systemic failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dori J. Maynard Award for Diversity in Journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Celebrates journalism that overcomes ignorance, stereotypes, intolerance, racism or hate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges value compelling, moving, beautifully told work that brings human perspective to contentious issues (example: a multi-chapter story with accompanying podcasts that humanizes families divided by the U.S.-Mexico border). The award is intended to recognize reporting that provides rare human looks at issues and their impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frank A. Blethen Award for Local Accountability Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes outstanding work done by a news organization that holds important local institutions accountable for their actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges reward deeply reported investigations that embed with affected communities, analyze large datasets/records, produce comparisons that expose systemic failures, and lead to measurable impact (e.g., policy changes, program creation, federal investigations). Winning example: series exposing failure of public school leaders that resulted in magnet programs, financial investments, and federal scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mike Royko Award for Commentary/Column Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in writing by an individual that expresses a personal point of view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria include deeply reported and gracefully written columns that harness the columnist's voice to speak for and to the community, capture emotion (grief, outrage, bravery), and address complex subject matter with eloquence and strong reporting. Winning examples demonstrate personal perspective combined with reporting and eloquent civic engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punch Sulzberger Award for Online Storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence and innovation in the use of digital tools to tell news stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges value digital storytelling that is a seamless, immersive experience and that uses multimedia elements with purpose and precision to enhance and drive the story. Examples include thoughtful use of video and audio to demonstrate arguments, 3-D modeling and video to create immersive tours, and multimedia packages that clearly illustrate key points of critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breaking News Writing Award
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded for coverage of breaking news events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges look for accurate, trustworthy, comprehensive and up-to-the-minute coverage; clear, crisp writing and sharp editing; stories packed with key information and told free of clutter; and reporting informed by deep institutional knowledge of the community and context. Winning example: coverage of Freddie Gray death and ensuing riots credited for breadth of staff deployment and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community Service Photojournalism Award
rubrics_metrics.description: Rewards photography that captures the sense of a community with powerful and meaningful images and provides an understanding of the community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges seek photo work that goes beyond predictable scenes to capture moments that reveal passion and complexity, creating understanding of community events and issues. Winning examples included haunting and dramatic images from protests that revealed nuance beyond typical coverage.
